key_insight: A gut microbiome-derived score built from 28 species was associated with higher future cancer risk years before diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this kind of microbiome signal could help identify people at elevated cancer risk for earlier surveillance or prevention research.
method: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from 5,997 participants in population-based cohorts.
Built a microbiome risk score using 28 microbial species and linked it to longitudinal cancer registry outcomes.
Tested the score in independent external case-control datasets and a separate population cohort.
evidence_signal: Higher microbiome risk scores were associated with incident cancer over up to 10 years of follow-up (adjusted HR per 1-SD increase, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.44-1.82), with replication in external datasets.
watch_item: This is association-based evidence, so the score is not yet a proven clinical test and may be influenced by confounding, cohort differences, or limited generalizability.
paper_title: A gut microbiome-derived risk score is associated with future cancer development
